defects.summary: RecursionError from deeply nested JSON escapes `except ValueError` at plain json.loads sites that read child-process output, project files and analyst annotations
defects.failure_scenario: A Ghidra extractor child that parsed a hostile binary prints one stdout line starting with "{" followed by 60,000 "[" (inside the 64 KiB STDOUT_LIMIT), or a shared project carries a match-override annotation whose text is 20,000 "[": `_child_documents`, `read_manifest` and `reports._annotation` raise RecursionError instead of UnifiedError/PT-* (run this session: "ESCAPED RecursionError", "ir.reader.read_manifest -> RecursionError", "reports._annotation -> RecursionError"). The unified run or report export ends as an untyped runtime error (CLI exit 3 with "RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded"); no memory corruption.
defects.proposed_fix: Route each site through persistence.strict_json (already depth-safe) or add RecursionError to the except tuple; keep the typed PT-* error of each module. Leave backend.py and unified/sources/** to their lane owners.
defects.regression_test: New tests/test_json_recursion_boundaries.py: parametrized over the entry points with "[" * 60000 and '{"a":' * 60000; each must raise the module's typed error or return its "unreadable" value, never RecursionError.

defects.summary: Process-group kill is sent after the group leader was reaped (pid reuse window)
defects.failure_scenario: A child exits normally; `child.poll()` reaps it; before terminate() runs the pid is recycled to a new process-group leader owned by the same user; os.killpg kills that unrelated group. Needs pid wrap-around inside milliseconds (UNVERIFIED in practice).
defects.proposed_fix: POSIX: detect exit with os.waitid(P_PID, pid, WEXITED | WNOWAIT) so the leader stays a zombie (pid cannot be recycled) while killpg runs, then reap; skip the kill in `finally` once the child is reaped.
defects.regression_test: tests/test_jobs.py: wrap os.killpg and assert every call happens while child.returncode is None (leader not yet reaped); existing descendant-kill tests stay green.

defects.summary: Offline-bundle ZIP member cap is enforced after zipfile has materialised every central-directory entry
defects.failure_scenario: A user selects a hostile archive with millions of tiny central-directory records: memory proportional to entry count is allocated before "too many members" is reported. Bounded by the archive size the user chose.
defects.proposed_fix: Read the EOCD / ZIP64 EOCD total-entries field from the tail of the file and refuse above MAX_MEMBERS + 1 before constructing ZipFile.
defects.regression_test: tests/test_offline_bundle.py: archive with MAX_MEMBERS + 2 entries is refused while zipfile.ZipFile is monkeypatched to fail if constructed; ZIP64 variant; honest bundle still inspects.

defects.summary: safe_path accepts Windows device names and trailing dot/space components
defects.failure_scenario: An attacker-edited project snapshot sets AnalysisRun.raw_path to "runs/x/CON" or "runs/x/raw.json." ; on Windows the path resolves to the console device or to a different file than the one named. Other persisted paths are hash-derived. Not exercisable on Linux as an exploit, but the string rule is platform-neutral.
defects.proposed_fix: Reuse the offline_bundle._safe_relative component rules (WINDOWS_RESERVED, trailing dot/space) inside safe_path on every platform.
defects.regression_test: tests/test_core.py or tests/test_hostile_input_fuzz_regressions.py: parametrized safe_path refusals for CON, nul.txt, COM1, "a./b", "a /b"; existing artifacts/<sha>.bin paths still accepted.

defects.summary: Windows child environment block is built without rejecting NUL or "=" in names/values
defects.failure_scenario: A configured path or passthrough value containing NUL would terminate its entry early and inject a further NAME=value pair into the child environment. Values come from os.environ and configured paths, which cannot hold NUL on Windows today.
defects.proposed_fix: Validate env in run_process before spawning on every platform: reject NUL in keys/values and "=" or empty keys with a PT-BACKEND ValueError.
defects.regression_test: tests/test_jobs.py: run_process with env {"A": "x\0B=y"} and {"A=B": "x"} raises ValueError matching PT-BACKEND before any spawn (spawn function monkeypatched to fail if reached).

defects.summary: Redirect allowlist admits any Azure storage account
defects.failure_scenario: A spoofed symbol server redirects to an attacker-owned *.blob.core.windows.net account: the attacker learns the client IP and can drip a body; content is still rejected by the Winbindex SHA-256 and size check.
defects.proposed_fix: Pin the Microsoft symbol shard host pattern once confirmed from live traffic.
defects.regression_test: Loopback/fake-opener test that a non-pinned blob host is refused (after the data decision).

defects.summary: Authenticode probe is given a path, not the verified handle
defects.failure_scenario: A writer in the project folder swaps the file between VerifiedArtifactReader verification and WinVerifyTrust; the trust verdict describes other bytes. Windows only.
defects.proposed_fix: Verify on a handle or re-hash after the probe.
defects.regression_test: Windows-only test with a swap hook between hash and probe.

defects.summary: tier_w PE view reads a whole RVA range in one call and leaks ArtifactBytesError
defects.failure_scenario: A Tier W local run over a real image whose .reloc or .pdata is larger than 16 MiB raises ArtifactBytesError("read_too_large") out of PeView.read_rva; callers that catch PeTableError (the module contract) crash the labelling run for that binary.
defects.proposed_fix: Read in MAX_READ_BYTES pieces and map ArtifactBytesError to PeTableError, as pe_overview/tables.py does (commit 9957da8).
defects.regression_test: tests/test_tier_w_pe.py: a directory larger than one read is read in pieces; a failed read is a PeTableError.

defects.summary: tier_w relocation reader appends one warning per unknown-type entry
defects.failure_scenario: A crafted .reloc with millions of type-7 entries grows PeView.warnings to millions of strings (memory, and any report that prints them).
defects.proposed_fix: Warn once per type (set of seen kinds).
defects.regression_test: tests/test_tier_w_pe.py: 100,000 unknown-type entries give one warning per type.

defects.summary: Unified IR treats a 16-32 MiB relocation directory as unreadable
defects.failure_scenario: An image whose base-relocation directory is between MAX_READ_BYTES (16 MiB) and MAX_RELOC_DIRECTORY (32 MiB): `_Rva.read` asks the reader for one over-size read, the ArtifactBytesError is swallowed and the tables carry `reloc-unreadable` and zero relocations although the directory is inside the documented cap; relocation-aware address facts are lost for that side (downstream effect on verdicts UNVERIFIED).
defects.proposed_fix: Split each mapped range into MAX_READ_BYTES pieces inside `_Rva.read`.
defects.regression_test: tests/test_unified_ir_pe_tables.py: a 17 MiB directory of valid blocks yields relocations and no `reloc-unreadable` (or `reloc-cap` when over MAX_RELOCATIONS).

defects.summary: Import caps are checked before the terminating entry is read
defects.failure_scenario: A valid import table with exactly 512 DLL descriptors and a zero terminator is reported truncated (`import_dlls_over_cap`), which makes api_delta and PeTables.import_slots report "unavailable" for a complete table.
defects.proposed_fix: At the cap, read the next entry and only warn/truncate when it is not the terminator (same for 4096 per DLL and 20000 total).
defects.regression_test: tests/test_pe_overview.py: 511, 512 (not truncated) and 513 (truncated) descriptors.

defects.summary: Hand-written sanitisers diverge from hostile_text.is_hostile

defects.summary: A failed thread start leaves the channel busy forever

defects.summary: generate_schemas.py ignores arguments and always rewrites
